display_name: Immigration Act 1971 (UK) under one top-level goal — right of abode and the need for leave to enter, continuation of leave under s 3C, and for ss 24 and 24B offences the maximum sentences and the s 28 extended time limits — and those three goals

others: the leave is extended by s 3C under … on (ia71-status.l4)
the maximum on summary conviction for (ia71-offences.l4)
the last day to lay an information for (ia71-offences.l4)

scope: Goal-focused, at the user's direction: ss 1(1)-(3), 2(1), 3(1), 3ZA, 3C(1)-(3), 24(A1)-(G1), (1), (3)-(3A), 24B(3)-(4), 28(1)(a), (1A)(a) of the revised text as at 5 January 2026. Which offence was committed is an input (its elements are not encoded). Left out on purpose: leave and conditions, deportation, exemptions, ETAs, appeals, other offences, powers, Schedules.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-18 (tests-independent.l4, 98 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read); none failed. It noted that the brief's 'which offence is committed' is not encoded — the offence is an input — and NOTES says so. Dates are computed as the Act words them, with no working-day rule. The pipeline has not been run.

forks.F1: s 1(3)/3ZA(5): local journey needs no leave except an excluded Irish citizen.
forks.F2: s 3C(1)(b): application on the last day of leave counts.
forks.F3: s 3C(2): extended while undecided or up to the last day of appeal/review rights; not on or after departure.
forks.F4: s 24(F1)(a), (G1): general limit and transition as inputs.
forks.F5: s 24B(4): 51 weeks unless the input says the offence predates s 281(5) CJA 2003.
forks.F6: s 28(1)(a): later of six months after and the earlier of three years after and two months after the certified date.
forks.F7: s 28(1A)(a): later end of six months beginning with offence and three months beginning with first arrest.
forks.F8: No extended limit for C1, (1)(b), 24B: NOTHING.
